title: PLANT CELL
coreFormula: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living things!
description: A complete breakdown of plant cell anatomy, specialized organelles (Cell Wall, Chloroplast, Central Vacuole), and cellular machinery.

properties.name: Cell Membrane
properties.explanation: Thin layer that surrounds the cell. It provides structure and protection and it is semi-permeable.
properties.example: Acts like a smart security gatekeeper with turnstiles. For example, when you water a plant, the membrane opens microscopic channels to let water and vital minerals flow in while blocking harmful bacteria and toxins from getting inside.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: The security gatekeeper of the cell!

properties.name: Cytoplasm
properties.explanation: The fluid in which organelles are suspended. It maintains the pressure inside of the cell.
properties.example: Functions like a nutrient-rich, shock-absorbing gel filling a water balloon. For example, it cushions the organelles so they do not crash into each other, and lets dissolved sugars and enzymes float smoothly across the cell to wherever reactions occur.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Cyto = Cell, Plasm = Fluid matrix!

properties.name: Mitochondria
properties.formula: Cellular Respiration: Glucose + O₂ → ATP Energy
properties.explanation: Nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell because they provide energy for the cell. The site of cellular respiration.
properties.example: Acts like an internal power plant or turbine generator. For example, whenever the plant needs energy to open flower petals or push roots through soil, the mitochondria burn stored glucose sugar with oxygen to create bursts of ATP energy packets.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Mighty Mitochondria = Powerhouse!

properties.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum
properties.explanation: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum makes lipids (fats), modifies proteins and transports them throughout the cell.
properties.example: Operates like a chemical manufacturing line and internal highway. For example, it synthesizes lipids (essential fats and oils that form waterproof leaf wax coatings) and pipes these newly made fats through smooth winding tubules directly to cell parts that need repair.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Smooth ER makes smooth lipids and highways!

properties.name: Golgi Body
properties.explanation: Packages proteins and carbohydrates into vesicles for transport outside of the cell.
properties.example: Works like a post office and packaging distribution center (like FedEx/Amazon). For example, it receives newly made proteins, wraps them into tiny shipping bubbles called vesicles, prints chemical address tags on them, and ships them out to build plant cell walls or nectar.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Golgi = 'Go' deliver the packages!

properties.name: Nucleus & Nucleolus
properties.explanation: The control center of the cell that directs functions and contains DNA. The nucleolus aids in the production of ribosomes.
properties.example: Functions as the master command center and architectural DNA library. For example, its chromosomes store the complete master recipe manual instructing the cell when to grow, repair damage, and divide; meanwhile, the dense nucleolus inside acts like a machine shop assembling ribosomes.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Nucleus = Brain / Boss of the cell!

properties.name: Rough ER & Ribosomes
properties.explanation: Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes bound to its membranes. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
properties.example: Operates like a heavy-duty protein construction factory. For example, the tiny ribosomes studded all over the rough ER read genetic messenger recipes and snap amino acids together like LEGO bricks to build sturdy structural proteins and digestive enzymes.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Ribosomes make Ribs (Proteins)!

properties.name: Cell Wall
properties.explanation: Found only in plant cells, cell walls provide extra structure and protection for the cell's internal structures.
properties.example: Acts like a rigid outer suit of armor and fortress brick wall made of tough cellulose fibers. For example, it gives plant stems the strong structural backbone needed so giant trees and tall sunflowers can stand straight up against gravity and wind without having bones.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Like a fortress wall outside a castle!

properties.name: Central Vacuole
properties.explanation: Vacuoles provide storage for materials such as water. A plant cell's vacuole is larger than in an animal cell.
properties.example: Functions like a giant pressurized water storage reservoir. For example, when you water a drooping wilted plant, this vacuole fills up like an inflated water balloon, pushing outward against the cell wall (turgor pressure) to make stems and leaves stand stiff and crisp.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Vacuole is like a giant water reservoir!

properties.name: Chloroplast
properties.explanation: Convert light energy from the sun into sugars that can be used for energy in a process called photosynthesis.
properties.example: Operates like miniature solar panels and a food-cooking kitchen. For example, green chlorophyll pigments inside trap rays of sunlight and mix that solar energy with water and carbon dioxide gas (photosynthesis) to cook sweet glucose sugar for plant food and release fresh oxygen into the air.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Solar panels of the plant world!

quiz.q: According to the teacher notes, which organelle is a thin, semi-permeable layer that surrounds the cell, providing structure and protection?
options: Cell Membrane
Cell Wall
Cytoplasm
Endoplasmic Reticulum
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Thin layer that surrounds the cell. It provides structure and protection and it is semi-permeable.'

quiz.q: In the worksheet explanation, what is the fluid in which organelles are suspended that maintains pressure inside the cell?
options: Cytoplasm
Central Vacuole
Nucleoplasm
Mitochondria
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'The fluid in which organelles are suspended. It maintains the pressure inside of the cell.'

quiz.q: Why are Mitochondria nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' in the teacher notes?
options: Because they provide energy for the cell and are the site of cellular respiration
Because they store water and minerals
Because they package proteins into vesicles
Because they make the cell look green
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell because they provide energy for the cell. The site of cellular respiration.'

quiz.q: What does the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum do according to the teacher explanation?
options: Makes lipids (fats), modifies proteins and transports them throughout the cell
Performs photosynthesis using light photons
Synthesizes DNA in the control center
Builds the rigid outer cell wall
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Smooth endoplasmic reticulum makes lipids (fats), modifies proteins and transports them throughout the cell.'

quiz.q: According to the notes, what is the exact function of the Golgi Body?
options: Packages proteins and carbohydrates into vesicles for transport outside of the cell
Directs cell division and stores chromosomes
Stores water to keep plant stems upright
Absorbs solar energy to make glucose
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Packages proteins and carbohydrates into vesicles for transport outside of the cell.'

quiz.q: What is described as the control center of the cell that directs functions, contains DNA, and has a nucleolus that aids in making ribosomes?
options: Nucleus & Nucleolus
Central Vacuole
Golgi Body
Rough ER
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'The control center of the cell that directs functions and contains DNA. The nucleolus aids in the production of ribosomes.'

quiz.q: According to the teacher notes, what makes Rough ER 'rough' and what is its role?
options: It has ribosomes bound to its membranes, which are the site of protein synthesis
It has coarse cellulose crystals that protect the nucleus
It has jagged edges to tear up waste materials
It is rough from storing sharp mineral crystals
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes bound to its membranes. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.'

quiz.q: Which protective structure is found ONLY in plant cells to provide extra structure and protection for internal structures?
options: Cell Wall
Cell Membrane
Cytoplasm
Mitochondria
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Found only in plant cells, cell walls provide extra structure and protection for the cell\'s internal structures.'

quiz.q: In the teacher notes, how does a plant cell's vacuole compare to an animal cell's vacuole?
options: A plant cell's vacuole is larger and provides storage for materials like water
Plant cells do not have vacuoles at all
Plant vacuoles only store air, while animal vacuoles store water
They are identical in size and function
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Vacuoles provide storage for materials such as water. A plant cell\'s vacuole is larger than in an animal cell.'

quiz.q: According to the worksheet notes, what do Chloroplasts convert and what process do they use?
options: Convert light energy from the sun into sugars for energy in photosynthesis
Convert water into oxygen gas through respiration
Convert proteins into lipids through active transport
Convert sound waves into chemical signals
quiz.why: Teacher note: 'Convert light energy from the sun into sugars that can be used for energy in a process called photosynthesis.'

title: ANIMAL CELL (BASIC UNIT OF LIFE)
description: Learn about the Animal Cell Parts and Organelle Functions

properties.name: Cell Membrane
properties.explanation: Thin layer that surrounds the cell . It provides structure and protection and it is semi-permeable.
properties.example: Functions like a flexible, selective border patrol surrounding the animal cell. For example, in your muscle and skin cells, it opens tiny doorways to allow glucose sugar and oxygen in while pumping carbon dioxide and waste out, keeping toxic chemicals out.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: The security gatekeeper of the cell!

properties.name: Cytoplasm
properties.explanation: The fluid in which organelles are suspended. It maintains the pressure inside of the cell.
properties.example: Acts like a jelly-like shock absorber and biochemical pool. For example, when you jump or run, the fluid cytoplasm cushions your cell's delicate organelles against physical impact and maintains internal turgor pressure so the cell maintains its proper shape.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Cyto = Cell, Plasm = Fluid matrix!

properties.name: Mitochondria
properties.explanation: Nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell because they provide the energy for the cell. The site of cellular respiration.
properties.example: Operates as the cellular powerhouse and energy turbine. For example, during gym class when you sprint, your heart and muscle cell mitochondria consume the sugar from your meals and oxygen from your lungs to generate millions of ATP energy fuel sparks every second.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Mighty Mitochondria = Powerhouse!

properties.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum
properties.explanation: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum makes lipids (fats), modifies protein and transports them throughout the cell.
properties.example: Serves as a detoxification laboratory and lipid highway. For example, in liver cells, the smooth ER breaks down medicines, alcohol, and harmful pollutants to detoxify your bloodstream, while also synthesizing essential cell fats, steroids, and cholesterol.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Smooth ER makes smooth lipids and highways!

properties.name: Golgi Body
properties.explanation: Packages proteins and carbohydrates into vesicles for transport outside of the cell.
properties.example: Functions like a sorting and packaging depot. For example, in your salivary gland cells, the Golgi body wraps digestive enzymes into membrane-bound vesicle packages and exports them out of the cell into your saliva to help dissolve food as you chew.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Golgi = 'Go' deliver the packages!

properties.name: Nucleus & Nucleolus
properties.explanation: Control center of the cell that directs functions and contains DNA. The nucleolus aids in the production of ribosomes.
properties.example: Functions as the master headquarters holding your genetic code (DNA). For example, it contains your unique hereditary chromosomes that determine eye color, hair type, and instruct white blood cells how to fight germs; the nucleolus inside manufactures ribosome workers.
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Nucleus = Brain / Boss of the cell!

properties.name: Rough ER & Ribosomes
properties.explanation: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum has ribosomes bound to its membranes. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
properties.example: Operates like an automated protein factory floor. For example, ribosomes on the rough ER translate RNA instructions into collagen (which keeps your skin elastic and heals cuts) and antibodies (which hunt down and destroy invading viruses).
properties.trick: Memory Trick: Ribosomes make Ribs (Proteins)!

quiz.q: What is the core principle behind Animal Cell (basic unit of life)?
options: Cell is the basic unit of life that carries out all living functions
Cells are only found in non-living objects
Cells do not need energy or oxygen
Cells are destroyed whenever they divide
quiz.why: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms!

quiz.q: Why is the Mitochondria nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell?
options: Because they provide the energy for the cell (site of cellular respiration)
Because they make lipids and fats
Because they store water like a vacuole
Because they contain DNA in the nucleus
quiz.why: Mitochondria produce ATP energy for cellular functions!

title: MULTICELLULAR ORGANISMS
coreFormula: an organism made of two or more cells

properties.name: Multicellular Organisms
properties.formula: an organism made with two or more cells
properties.explanation:
• These organisms are able to be seen with the naked eye
• These organisms need all parts of themselves to survive
• Plants belong to the category of autotrophs, meaning self feeders
• In the kingdom Animalia; Heterotrophic - other feeder, organisms that eat other organisms.
properties.example: Functions through teamwork and division of labor between specialized cells. For example, inside a human body or a tree, billions of specialized cells work together: red blood cells deliver oxygen, muscle cells contract to create motion, and root cells absorb water—no single cell could survive alone, but together they form living tissues, organs, and body systems that keep the entire organism alive!
properties.trick: Multi = many cells working together to survive!

quiz.q: What is a multicellular organism?
options: an organism made of two or more cells
an organism made of only 1 cell.
an organism that moves only with pseudopodia
an organism without any living cells
quiz.why: Multicellular organisms are composed of two or more cells and need all parts to survive!

quiz.q: In multicellular plants, what does 'autotroph' mean?
options: self feeders (plants that make their own food)
Heterotrophic - other feeder, organisms that eat other organisms
an organism made of only 1 cell.
organisms that move by using a flagellum
quiz.why: Plants belong to the category of autotrophs, meaning self feeders!

quiz.q: In the kingdom Animalia, what does 'heterotrophic' mean?
options: Other feeder (organisms that eat other organisms)
Self feeders (organisms that make their own food)
An organism made of only 1 cell.
Organisms that move by cillia (hair like)
quiz.why: In the kingdom Animalia, animals are heterotrophic and eat other organisms!

title: UNICELLULAR ORGANISM
coreFormula: an organism made of only 1 cell.
description: Examples of unicellular organisms: Amoeba (pseudopodia), Bacteria, Euglena (flagellum, and paramecium (cilla). Other types of unicellular organisms come from the kingdom Protista. Examples of protists include algae, Amoeba, Paramecium, volvox, amd Euglena. Algae are plantlike protists and they contain chlorophyll.

properties.name: Euglena
properties.formula: an organism made of only 1 cell.
properties.explanation: Move by using  a flagellum (thread like structures that whip around).
properties.example: Functions like a microscopic, self-steering solar submarine. For example, it senses light with a red eyespot and whips a long, thread-like flagellum like an outboard motor propeller to swim toward sunlit pond water, where its green chloroplasts make food through photosynthesis (or it absorbs dissolved nutrients if trapped in the dark).
properties.trick: Flagellum whips like a propeller!

properties.name: Volvox
properties.formula: an organism made of only 1 cell.
properties.explanation: They move by using a flagellum ( thread like structures that whip around).
properties.example: Functions like a synchronized swimming sphere. For example, up to 50,000 individual green algal cells join together into a hollow globe; by beating their paired flagella in synchronized harmony, they roll the entire spherical colony through pond water toward sunlight like a living green wheel.
properties.trick: Volvox colonies roll with flagella!

properties.name: Paramecium
properties.formula: an organism made of only 1 cell.
properties.explanation: A paramecium moves by cillia (hair like)
properties.example: Functions like a microscopic slipper-shaped boat powered by thousands of tiny oars. For example, thousands of microscopic hair-like cilia covering its outer body paddle in coordinated waves to dart smoothly forward and backward through pond water, while sweeping bacteria into its oral groove mouth to eat.
properties.trick: Cilia paddle like tiny oars!

properties.name: Amoeba
properties.formula: an organism made of only 1 cell.
properties.explanation: An amoeba moves by projecting out its cytoplasm. These projections are called pseudopodia (false feet).
properties.example: Functions as a shape-shifting crawler and microscopic predator. For example, when it moves or hunts, it extends its fluid cytoplasm forward into temporary bulging arms called pseudopodia ('false feet') to crawl over rocks, and wraps two pseudopodia arms completely around bacteria to engulf and digest them inside a food vacuole.
properties.trick: Pseudopodia means false feet!

quiz.q: What is a unicellular organism?
options: an organism made of only 1 cell.
an organism made of two or more cells
an organism with millions of organs
an organism that is visible to the naked eye
quiz.why: A unicellular organism is made of only 1 cell!

quiz.q: How does a Euglena move?
options: Moves by using a flagellum (thread-like whip structure)
Moves by using cilia (tiny hair-like oars)
Moves by projecting out cytoplasm into pseudopodia
It uses roots to anchor itself
quiz.why: Euglena moves using a whip-like flagellum!

quiz.q: How does a Paramecium move?
options: Moves by using cilia (tiny hair-like structures)
Moves by using a whip-like flagellum
Moves by projecting out cytoplasm into false feet
It floats without any moving structures
quiz.why: Paramecium moves using tiny hair-like cilia!

quiz.q: How does an Amoeba move?
options: Moves by projecting out cytoplasm in false feet (pseudopodia)
Moves by whipping a flagellum propeller
Moves by beating tiny cilia hairs
It swims with fins
quiz.why: Amoeba projects out its cytoplasm in false feet called pseudopodia!

quiz.q: How does a Volvox move?
options: Moves by rolling using coordinated flagella
Moves by beating tiny cilia hairs
Moves by extending cytoplasmic false feet
It does not move at all
quiz.why: Volvox cells move by beating their flagella!
